title: Warm-start degradation: prefetch + KV-throttle hotpatch for long-context multi-tenant workloads
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Several customers (anonymized: RetailAI, FinLedger, HealthSearch) reported sudden increases in first-token latency and sustained token/sec drop on long-context workloads (8k-32k) starting 2026-03-05 after a kernel-selector tweak. Regression affects Hosted and Dedicated clusters and surfaced in a Private deployment during customer upgrade. Root cause appears to be poorer KV cache utilization and late prefetch scheduling for multi-tenant multiplexed queues leading to warm-start stalls and reduced sustained throughput.
observed_metrics_summary: TTFT median increased from 40ms -> 220ms for affected requests; tokens/sec per GPU fell 35% under mixed-length traffic. Error rate unchanged. Regression correlated with kernel-selector change deployed 2026-03-04 (canary->prod).
steps_taken: 2026-03-05 09:30 UTC: Pager escalation from Support; formed incident working group (Runtime + Infra + PM)
2026-03-05 11:00 UTC: Short-term mitigation - increased per-worker prefetch window on canary to improve KV hit rate (observed partial improvement)
2026-03-06 02:00 UTC: Rolled back kernel-selector heuristic change in one Dedicated pool; saw TTFT drop return to baseline for that pool
2026-03-07 07:00 UTC: Implemented emergency KV-throttle patch to prioritize warm-request KV prefetch in multiplex queues across Hosted fleet (gradual rollout)
2026-03-09 21:00 UTC: Conducted microbenchmarks showing warm-prefetch improves median TTFT by ~120ms but increases peak GPU memory pressure by ~6%
2026-03-11 10:00 UTC: Deployed short-lived fallback policy to route long-context requests to fallback model-variant with smaller kv-residency on contention
perf_before_after: Baseline (2026-03-03): median TTFT 40ms, tokens/sec 1.0k per GPU. Regression (2026-03-05): median TTFT 220ms, tokens/sec 650. Post-hotpatch (2026-03-10): median TTFT 95ms, tokens/sec 880. Numbers are fleet-aggregated for affected clusters.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Aggressive prefetch reduces TTFT but increases memory pressure and can cause OOM on older GPU types in Dedicated private deployments. KV-throttle reduces contention but may increase tail latency for very short requests. Permanent changes require tuning per-hardware profiles and may necessitate quantization/packing adjustments.
decision_log: 2026-03-06: Decided to rollback kernel-selector heuristic rollback in full (ENG-127800) after pilot rollback recovered metrics
2026-03-07: Approved emergency KV-throttle + prefetch hotpatch to stabilize customer experience; flagged for follow-up permanent fix
2026-03-09: Rejected immediate global aggressive prefetch due to memory risk on a subset of Dedicated GPU types; instead use adaptive per-pool thresholds
permanent_fix_plan: 1) Rework kernel-selector to include dynamic context-length-awareness and historical KV hit rates. 2) Implement adaptive prefetch that scales with available GPU memory and model variant. 3) Add simulator tests to catch warm-start regressions in CI. 4) CV-led rollout with telemetry gates and per-pool thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Fleet median TTFT for long-context requests <= 80ms on targeted HW tiers. 2) tokens/sec within 10% of baseline for mixed workloads. 3) No OOM incidents in Dedicated/private test pools. 4) Canary stability for 48h before wide rollout.
